title: Map values to training bands
scenario: Delvori Logistics is pricing 30 invented shipments using ascending lower-bound mass bands. Each band includes its lower bound and continues up to the next bound; duplicate masses are valid observations. A negative mass is invalid and must not match a price band.

lesson.intro: Approximate matching implements a stated interval rule. Lower-bound tables use the exact match or next smaller key; upper-bound tables require a different mode.

functions.name: XLOOKUP
functions.purpose: Find a key and return its corresponding value.
functions.arguments: Supply the key, aligned key and return ranges, optional missing label, match mode (0 exact, -1 next smaller, 1 next larger), and search direction (1 first, -1 last).
functions.mistake: Exact is the default. A first match does not aggregate duplicates. Binary search requires correctly sorted keys.

functions.name: MATCH
functions.purpose: Find the relative position of a value.
functions.arguments: lookup_value is the key; lookup_array is one row or column; use match_type 0 for exact matching.
functions.useCase: Find a row or column position for INDEX.
functions.mistake: Omitting 0 requests approximate matching, which has ordering requirements.

lesson.combine: Reuse IF to exclude negative mass and ROUND for freight cost. MATCH with type 1 requires ascending lower bounds. XLOOKUP match_mode -1 expresses exact-or-next-smaller; avoid binary search unless ordering is guaranteed.

tasks.prompt: Return Rate_CAD_per_km for the first shipment’s mass using the stated lower-bound bands.
Return the first mass’s 1-based band position within Bands!A2:A5.
For the first six shipments, return the rate for each nonnegative mass and Invalid for negative mass.
For the first shipment, calculate Distance_km times the matched rate, rounded to cents.

bonus.prompt: Return Rate_CAD_per_km for a hypothetical 99.9 kg shipment.
